local_facts.title: One whiteout closed US-131 for five hours
local_facts.claim: On Monday 19 January 2026 northbound US-131 was closed from West Main Street to Exit 38, including the US-131 Business Loop, after a chain of crashes involving at least fifteen vehicles including semi trucks. Strong winds and lake-effect snow showers had produced whiteout conditions. The closure began after 10:30 a.m. and the road reopened at 4 p.m.; tow trucks spent the afternoon pulling semis off the guardrails. MDOT and the Kalamazoo County Sheriff's Office reported the closure.
local_facts.why_it_matters: In a lake-effect event every recovery truck in the county is on the freeway. A car in a ditch on a side road waits behind the semis, and the honest arrival estimate on a day like that is hours, not minutes. Drivers should be told that number rather than a promise nobody can keep.

local_facts.title: The city, not the wrecker, sets the police-tow ceiling
local_facts.claim: Chapter 40 of the Kalamazoo City Code, titled Wreckers, provides that the City Commission shall establish by resolution and/or contract the maximum amounts which may be charged for any towing or wrecker service, including storage of any vehicle in the city regardless of where the tow originated, and that it is unlawful to demand payment in excess of a fee so established. The City Clerk's office (337-8792) holds the current permitted fees.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A police-ordered tow inside Kalamazoo has a legal price ceiling. A tow the driver calls for is a private transaction with no ceiling, which is why the price must be stated before the hook goes on rather than discovered on the invoice.

local_facts.title: Seventy-plus inches a year, most of it in three months
local_facts.claim: NOAA 1991-2020 climate normals measured at Gerald R. Ford International Airport in Grand Rapids, the nearest first-order station, put annual snowfall at 77.6 inches, with December averaging 20.8 inches, January 22.6 and February 17.2. The Great Lakes Integrated Sciences and Assessments program describes southwest Michigan's snow as lake-effect, produced when cold westerly winds cross the open water of Lake Michigan.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Lake-effect snow falls in narrow bands, so one township can be buried while the next gets flurries. Trucks stage where the band is, batteries fail on the first hard-freeze morning, and the ditch along M-43 fills with cars every January. Winter is the towing season in this county.

local_facts.title: Michigan caps impound storage at the lesser of two rates
local_facts.claim: MCL 257.252i provides that when a vehicle towed at the direction of a police agency is released, the storage fee that may be collected is the lesser of the daily rate established by contract with the agency that authorized the tow or the daily rate charged by the storage facility. The abandoned-vehicle sections that follow give the owner twenty days from the date of the notice to redeem the vehicle or petition the court before it may be sold.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Storage accrues daily whether or not the insurer has called back. Getting to the lot quickly with the title or registration and photo ID, and asking for the itemized bill, is the difference between a small charge and a large one.

anchors.label: Impound storage after a police tow
anchors.detail: MCL 257.252i limits the storage fee on a released vehicle to the lesser of the daily rate in the contract with the police agency or the lot's own posted rate. The owner has twenty days from the abandonment notice to redeem or petition the court.
